chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Those who came before us used to say: There is neither emancipation nor divorce except after what the man possesses.

key_terms.طَلَاقَ: Divorce (talaq) — the Islamic procedure by which a husband dissolves a marriage through a formal pronouncement
key_terms.عَتَاقَ: Emancipation or manumission — the act of freeing an enslaved person; a legal category in Islamic law with specific conditions and formulas
key_terms.يَمْلِكُ: Possesses/owns — refers here to the man having legal ownership or marital possession; the legal threshold required for effective pronouncements

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the conditions for valid divorce and emancipation in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports a legal principle held by earlier authorities: that the emancipation of a slave and the pronouncement of divorce are only effective after the husband or master actually has ownership or full marital possession. This ruling addresses jurisprudential questions about the conditions under which such legal declarations take effect. The historical context reflects debates among early Muslim jurists about whether acts of legal consequence require prior possession or capacity, and the Imam's citation of this principle indicates its authoritative standing in the tradition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Shuayb Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The ones<sup>asws</sup> before us<sup>asws</sup> were saying: ‘There is neither emancipation nor a divorce except after what the man owns’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Shu’ayb ibn Ya‘qub who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Those who were before us would say, ‘Setting free of a slave or divorce does not have any valid effect until a man has an ownership and marriage.’”
